emma_support: Heads up — escalation from a customer using JSON 'structured' mode. Their pydantic consumer is failing with JSONDecodeError. They say the API response includes an escaped JSON string instead of raw JSON object. Repro steps attached.

emma_support: Repro from customer (redacted):
```http
POST /v1/generate
Content-Type: application/json
Body:
{
  \"mode\": \"structured\",
  \"schema\": { \"type\": \"object\", \"properties\": { \"name\": { \"type\": \"string\" }, \"address\": {\"type\":\"string\"} }, \"required\": [\"name\",\"address\"] },
  \"prompt\": \"Return JSON with name and address. address includes newline.\"
}
```

emma_support: Customer says when they do `pydantic.parse_raw(resp.text)` it throws pointing at the opening quote. Their `resp.text` looks like:
```json
"{\"name\": \"Alice\", \"address\": \"123 Fake St.\nApt 4\"}"
```

emma_support: Note there's an extra wrapping quote — looks like we returned a JSON string containing the JSON, i.e. double-serialized. Customer expects a JSON object.

tom_eng: Thanks — can you paste the raw gateway body / headers we returned? Need to see if we set content-type or accidentally stringify before sending.

emma_support: Pasting gateway log (sanitized):
```
[2025-10-03T14:17:01Z] outbound_response content-type: application/json
[2025-10-03T14:17:01Z] outbound_response body: "{\"name\": \"Alice\", \"address\": \"123 Fake St.\nApt 4\"}"
```

mei_ml: That log is the problem — body is a JSON string literal. Looks like the structured-output handler is calling json.dumps on text that was already serialized by the model output composer (stream assembler). Probably happening for model outputs that are generated as text but flagged structured.

raj_sre: Any recent deploys touching output encoding or streaming wrapper?

tom_eng: I deployed a small change last night that adjusts newline sanitization for streaming. Could have accidentally run `json.dumps` on the assembled payload in `serve/response.py:format_structured`. I'll roll back a quick patch to canary and test.

mei_ml: Quick workaround for customers: they can do `if resp.text.startswith('"'):
    parsed = json.loads(resp.text)  # unescape once
else:
    parsed = resp.json()` but obviously not ideal. We should fix server-side.

emma_support: Customer accepted workaround but wants ETA. Can we give an estimate?

tom_eng: I'll patch `format_structured` to check payload type before serializing and add unit tests for streaming+structured. If tests pass, canary deploy in 30-45m.

raj_sre: Add a request id log to the structured branch so we can trace any future hits. Also add an automatic regression test in the API integration suite that calls our public client plus pydantic.parse_raw to catch double-serialization.

mei_ml: Also check multipart/stream vs buffered response paths — I think the streaming assembler returns a `str` while buffered path returns `dict`, and we only handle one path. Good to standardize on returning dict up the stack.

emma_support: I'll reply to customer: ETA ~45m for canary, suggest workaround in the meantime and offer an account credit.

lintbot: deploybot: Canary rollout for commit abc123 to service response-service started (namespace: canary)

tom_eng: Canary looks clean on initial tests. Keeping an eye on latencies. Will promote when greens.

emma_support: Thanks team, I'll update ticket.

mei_ml: Follow-up item: add an automated eval that validates output against the declared schema using both `json.loads` and `pydantic` in CI to catch subtle encoding mismatches.

emma_support: Agreed — added to backlog.
